c0-frame.title: Frame the cycle
c0-frame.imperative: Set the cycle flavor (shotgun | compare | refine) in the top-level flavor field; the human picks, you may recommend. Shotgun: pure divergence, a deliberately challenging idea count (default ~20, human-set) as cheap one-liners, wild entries sanctioned, light excursions only. Compare: 2-5 candidates developed seriously with trade-offs, recommendation-led, excursions per candidate where earned. Refine: harden one direction, chase open threads, test load-bearing assumptions, tighten interfaces in deep-module terms. Seed the FIRST cycle from templates/EXPLORER_STARTING_QUESTIONS.template.md (the itch; for whom; what does done feel like; what already exists; what would make this pointless); later cycles seed from the ideas board's open threads. Record pass when framed.

q1.title: <point question for this cycle>
q1.imperative: <A point-question that advances the flavor's goal. Ask one at a time with a recommended answer; explore the codebase/web where it can answer; append follow-up questions and new branches as items; skip questions overcome by earlier answers. Record the idea/verdict as the finding; a negative verdict states what was and was NOT tested (scoped nulls).>

x1.title: <excursion dispatch: one named question>
x1.imperative: <An excursion answering ONE named question, recorded as an EXCURSION_BRIEF on the ideas board before dispatch (question; type research | prototype | design-it-twice; what 'answered' looks like; budget/stop conditions). Either side may initiate (human 'go look up X' or agent proposal), same brief. Dispatch as a BACKGROUND subagent via run_crew.py; run recover_crews.py before dispatch and before consolidation. On-ramp: the result lands in this cycle's record and the board before consolidation. A slow excursion at consolidation time is the human's call — wait, or consolidate with it logged as an open thread carried into the next cycle; never silently dropped. Skip this item if the cycle needs no excursion. Record the excursion's scoped verdict as the finding.>
